help_intro_text: The project portal is where you follow the progress of your project, approve proposals and write to the supplier. There is nothing to install – a web browser on a computer or a phone is enough. Every part is in the menu on the left; below you find what each one is for and how to use it.
help_checkpoints_text:
The steps of the project in the order they follow each other. Each shows its state – Not started, In progress or Done – and the planned date. A step with an arrow has a description of what it covers; click it to expand it. At the top is the overall progress (finished steps out of all).
You can get an e-mail when the state or the date of a step changes – turn it on in My account.
help_threads_text:
All written communication with the supplier, split into threads by topic.
• New topic: the “New thread” button – fill in the subject, priority and text, attach files if needed.
• Reply: open the thread, write into the box at the bottom and click “Send”.
• Every message shows its author: your messages are on the right marked “You”, messages of colleagues from your company on the left with their name, messages of the supplier on the left in a white box.
• Older messages load with the button at the top of the thread; new messages appear by themselves.
• You can close a solved thread (Thread status) and reopen it at any time.
• “Search communication” searches subjects and message texts.
Threads are shared with all colleagues who have an account for the project.
help_attachments_text: Attach files to a new thread or a reply with the “Attach files” button (you can pick several at once). The number of files, the allowed types and the maximum size are checked right when you pick them – if a file does not fit, the portal tells you why and which types are allowed. Remove a picked file with its cross.
help_contacts_text: The contact of the person who runs your project at the supplier (phone and e-mail can be clicked) and the company and billing details of the supplier.
help_support_text: Write a new message in Communication, or use the contact in Contacts. Forgot your password? Sign in with a code from your e-mail, or write to the supplier – they will set a new one.
login_forgotten_hint: Forgot your password? Switch to "Code by e-mail" or contact your supplier.
error_too_many_attempts: Too many sign-in attempts. Please try again in a moment.
overview_waiting_on_you_hint: The supplier waits for your answer
files_lead: All files you and the supplier sent in the threads, in one place. Click the topic to open the thread of a file.
files_empty: There are no files in the threads yet.
files_error: The files could not be loaded. Try refreshing the data.
supplier_contact_empty: The supplier has not filled in a contact person yet.
help_login_text:
You enter the portal with the link of your project. You can sign in in three ways: with your login name and password, with a one-time code sent to your e-mail, or with the link of an invitation.
Every person on your side should have an own account – ask the supplier for an account for a colleague. Messages and decisions then show who wrote them.
You stay signed in for 24 hours after your last activity, even if you close the window or the browser in between. Then you sign in again.
You cannot change your password or login name yourself – ask the supplier.
help_overview_text:
A summary of the project in one place:
• numbers at the top – progress in percent, how many threads wait for your answer, unread messages and the estimated completion (a click opens the related part),
• a yellow bar when an approval request is waiting for you,
• “What is new” – news since your last visit are highlighted; a click opens what they are about,
• the current step, the description of the project and the technologies used.
Opening the Overview marks the news as seen (the number in the menu disappears).
help_waiting_title: Waiting on you / Supplier is answering
help_waiting_text: Every open thread shows whose turn it is. “Waiting on you” means the supplier wrote the last message and is waiting for your answer. “Supplier is answering” means it is their turn. Unread messages from the supplier are marked by a red number in the menu and at the thread, and the thread has a red stripe.
help_files_text:
All files of the project in one place – from threads, updates and approval requests, yours and the supplier's, newest first. Each file shows its size, date, author and a link to where it comes from (a click opens it).
For security the download links expire after a while. If a link does not work, open Files again or click the refresh button at the top right.
help_layout_text:
The top left shows who is signed in (Client) and to which project (Project). The menu on the left contains all parts of the portal; the numbers next to the items show unread messages, news and requests waiting for approval, next to Progress the number of finished steps.
The button with three lines narrows the menu to icons; on a phone it slides the menu in, choosing an item hides it again.
The button with arrows at the top right loads the newest data – most of it refreshes by itself every 15 seconds anyway. The flag next to it switches the language of the portal.
Every part has its own address, so you can bookmark it and a reload of the page keeps you where you were.
help_notifications_text:
In My account you fill in your e-mail and choose what you want to be told about: a reply of the supplier, a changed state of a step, a changed date of a step, a new update, an approval request. Everything is off by default and you can turn it off again at any time. Without an e-mail the notifications cannot be turned on.
The e-mail contains only the title and a link to the portal, never the text of a message – you always read the content after signing in.
account_managed_by_supplier: The name, login name and password are managed by the supplier - write to them if they need changing. Without a password you sign in with a code by e-mail.
notifications_lead: Choose what we should e-mail you about. Everything is off by default. The e-mail never contains the message text – only the thread or step title and a link to the portal.
notify_replies_title: The supplier replies in a thread
notify_replies_hint: A new reply of the supplier in any thread of the project.
notify_checkpoint_status_hint: A project step starts or is done.
notify_checkpoint_dates_hint: The supplier sets, moves or removes the due date of a step.
notifications_need_email: Fill in an e-mail to turn notifications on.
notifications_save_failed: The settings could not be saved. Check the e-mail and try again.
login_code_lead: Enter the login name or the e-mail of your account. We will send you a one-time sign-in code.
login_code_hint: The code is sent only to the e-mail saved on the account. It is valid for 15 minutes and can be used once.
login_code_sent: If the account exists and has an e-mail, we have sent a six-digit code to it. Please check your spam folder too.
error_code_invalid: The code is wrong or has expired. Try again or send yourself a new one.
error_code_request_failed: The code could not be sent. Please try again in a moment.
error_link_invalid: The sign-in link is invalid, already used or expired. Sign in with your password or have a code sent by e-mail.
news_empty: Nothing new here in the last 90 days.
approvals_lead: Here the supplier asks for your approval - of a design, texts or a finished part, for example. Approving confirms they can go on; if something is not right, request changes with a comment.
approvals_empty: There are no approval requests yet.
approval_record_note: Your decision is saved with the account name and time, and the supplier is notified.
approval_comment_required: Please write what needs to change.
approval_decision_failed: The decision could not be saved. The request may have changed meanwhile - refresh the page and try again.
updates_lead: News from the supplier about what is done, what is happening now and what comes next.
updates_empty: The supplier has not published any update yet.
notify_updates_hint: A new progress report in the Updates section.
notify_approvals_hint: A new or reopened approval request.
account_signin_password_code: Password or code from the e-mail
account_signin_code: Code from the e-mail (no password set)
help_login_code_title: Signing in with a code or an e-mail link
help_login_code_text:
If your account has an e-mail, you do not need a password: on the sign-in page choose “Code by e-mail”, enter your login name or e-mail and type in the six-digit code from the e-mail. The code is valid for 15 minutes.
The invitation of the supplier contains a link that signs you in with one click. It is valid for 7 days and can be used only once. If you click it again while you are still signed in, the portal simply opens. Otherwise the sign-in page appears – sign in with a code or ask for a new invitation.
Using a code or a link confirms your e-mail.
help_approvals_text:
Here the supplier asks for your binding consent – to a proposal, texts or a finished part. The request shows a description, files, possibly the step of the project and the date by which you should decide.
• You agree? Click “Approve”.
• You want changes? Click “Request changes” and write what to change (the comment is required).
The decision is saved with your name and time and cannot be changed; the supplier is notified. After the changes the supplier may send the request again – the history of decisions stays with it. The orange number in the menu shows how many requests are waiting.
help_updates_text: News from the supplier about the progress – what is done, what is happening and what comes next, sometimes with files. The newest are at the top. New updates also appear in the Overview under “What is new”, and you can get them by e-mail.
help_maintenance_text: The supplier may switch the portal off for a short maintenance – you then see the “Maintenance in progress” page. Nothing is lost; try again in a while with “Try again” and the portal takes you back where you were.
help_security_text:
• On a shared or someone else's computer, log out when you finish (“Log out” at the bottom left).
• Do not forward sign-in codes, e-mail links or your password – every colleague should have an own account.
• The supplier will never ask you for your password or a code – if someone does, it is not the supplier.
• A code and an e-mail link are valid only for a short time and only once.
help_account_text:
The data of your account: name, login name, how you sign in and whether your e-mail is confirmed. These are managed by the supplier.
Here you set your e-mail, the language of the e-mails and the notifications yourself. “Save” stores the changes, “Cancel” returns the saved values.
help_account_switch_text:
In one browser only one account can be signed in to a project at a time. If a colleague signs in with their account in the same browser (for example with the link from their e-mail), the open portal windows switch to their account when you return to them – the top left always shows who is signed in (“Client: …”).
If two of you need to work at the same time, each use a different browser or a private (incognito) window.
help_first_steps_text:
1. Sign in with the link of your invitation (or with the login name and password the supplier gave you).
2. Open “My account” (bottom left), check your e-mail and turn on the notifications you want.
3. Look at the “Overview” – you will see what is new and what is waiting for you.
4. A question or documents to send? Start a new thread in “Communication”.
5. When you finish on a shared or someone else's computer, click “Log out” at the bottom left.
